sections.description: Granular, transparent WordPress performance optimisation across core, scripts, fonts, preloading, database, images, WooCommerce and multisite — plus per-page and per-template Used CSS, and paste-in Critical CSS.
sections.changelog:
1.23.1

  • Fix: activation and deactivation now actually run. The hooks were registered against the bootstrap file rather than the main plugin file, so WordPress never fired them — a fresh install created none of its database tables and scheduled no cron jobs, and deactivating left .htaccess blocks and caches behind. Existing installs are repaired automatically on upgrade.
  • Fix: WebP/AVIF .htaccess delivery now works when WordPress is installed in a subdirectory, where the rewrite condition previously never matched and every visitor silently received the original JPEG. If you had this enabled on a subdirectory site, toggle it off and on to write the corrected rules.
  • Fix: images could be wrapped in a <picture> element twice, producing nested markup, because more than one filter can see the same image. Wrapping is now idempotent and existing <picture> elements are left alone. The Gutenberg block filter also gained the context guard the other filters already had.
  • Fix: PHP 7.4 compatibility. The bundled Symfony CssSelector calls str_contains(), which is PHP 8.0+, and would fatal on 7.4 during a Used CSS analysis. Symfony's own polyfill dependency had not been vendored alongside it; it now is.
  • Security: TLS certificate verification is no longer disabled on outbound requests. The Google Fonts downloader writes its responses into the uploads directory, so those now verify with no fallback; requests to the site's own front end verify by default and fall back only for the site's own host, so self-signed staging certificates keep working.
  • Security: the bulk WebP/AVIF converters now resolve the submitted path and confirm it lands inside the uploads directory and is a supported image. Both endpoints already required a nonce and manage_options; this is defence in depth.
  • New: uninstall.php. Deleting the plugin removes its options, tables, scheduled events, transients and caches. Your Media Library is untouched, and generated WebP/AVIF files and self-hosted fonts are left in place since a cache or CDN may still reference them.
  • Housekeeping: removed three unreferenced JavaScript files and an obsolete bundled copy of the Plugin Update Checker (v5.6).

1.23.0

  • New: Used CSS Mode B — per-template critical CSS that genuinely removes the unused stylesheets rather than deferring them, so the bytes stop being downloaded at all. One cache entry per template instead of one per page. Off by default.
  • New: multi-sample template learning. Each template is learned from several distinct URLs and keeps the union of what they used, so a rule only one page needs still survives for the whole template. Learning visits are served untouched.
  • New: selector safelist — the guard rail for anything JavaScript adds after load (consent banners, cart drawers, modals, scroll-toggled classes), which a static analysis cannot see.
  • Safety: a stylesheet is only removed if that exact file was analysed while learning. Sheets carrying @import, print and narrow-media sheets, external sheets and excluded sheets are always left alone.
  • Safety: the inlined CSS replaces the first stylesheet it stands in for, preserving the original cascade position; media="screen" rules are re-wrapped so they cannot leak into print.
  • Change: Mode A, Async CSS and Combine CSS all stand down when Mode B is on — the modes are alternatives. Hand-pasted Critical CSS still takes precedence over both.
  • New: the Performance Doctor understands both modes, recommends one or the other but never both, and reports whether Mode B is working, still learning, or leaving sheets alone by design.
  • New: ?mbrpe_modeb=off serves a single request with its original stylesheets, for comparing against the optimised page.

1.22.1

  • New: the Performance Doctor now understands script modules — it counts them, reports where the import map and preload hints landed, and recommends preload hoisting when it would help.
  • New: import map ordering check. A module printed in the head while the map sits in the footer cannot resolve its bare specifier imports; the Doctor now flags this as high priority.
  • New: the Doctor tells apart hoisting off, hoisting still learning the URL, and hoisting working — and tells block themes plainly that core already handles it.
  • Note: the learned module map is keyed on plugin version, so this upgrade clears it by design. Hoisted hints resume from the second visit to each URL.

1.22.0

  • New: Script Modules and Interactivity API support (WP 6.5+), including module preload hoisting that fixes late preload hints on classic themes.
  • New: static dependency graph walking, fetchpriority control, preload cap and exclusions. Off by default.

1.21.3

  • Fix: PDF report preview now renders as a centred A4 sheet instead of stretching to the browser width.
  • Fix: Note badge styling in reports; proper tab names on recommendation links.

1.21.2

  • Fix: real-user field data now appears in the Doctor site-scan view (it was being stripped by the info-tier roll-up filter).
  • Change: field data reported once site-wide rather than per template, and provisional notes now show the actual readings.

1.21.1

  • Fix: RUM field data now reaches the Performance Doctor immediately via on-demand aggregation, rather than waiting for the nightly cron.
  • New: "Run aggregation now" button; clearer status reporting; provisional p75s shown from 10 samples.

1.21.0

  • New: self-hosted Real User Monitoring — collects real-user Core Web Vitals (LCP, CLS, INP) into local tables and shows field data per template and per URL. No cookies, no IPs, nothing leaves your server. Off by default.
  • Hardening: the plugin's own mbrpe/v1 REST namespace is always permitted through REST hardening so the RUM beacon works for logged-out visitors.

1.20.1

  • Update checks now served from GitHub for reliable delivery.
  • Consolidated self-hosted release; corrected update manifest.
sections.installation: Upload the plugin to /wp-content/plugins/, activate, and configure under MBR → Performance.
